analysis.title: BJ's Wholesale Club Holdings (BJ): First Take: 3Q top line and EPS beat, while gross margin came in below expectations; FY26 guidance raised
key_insights: BJ reported 3Q SSS (ex gas) of +4.1% vs GS +2.6% and consensus (LSEG) +2.8%. EBIT of $314mn vs GS $236mn and consensus $234mn. Adj. EPS of $1.73 vs GS $1.26 and consensus $1.25.
MFI (membership fee income) grew +9.5% y/y, which GS cites as evidence of a solid membership base.
FY26 guidance raised. SSS (ex gas) now +2.5-3.0%, up from +2.0-3.0% (GS/consensus +2.4%/+2.6%). Adj. EPS now $5.10-5.30, up from $4.60-4.80 (GS/consensus $4.80/$4.73).

Gross margin of 16.3% was below GS's consensus-aligned estimate of 18.2%, down 265 bps y/y. Merchandise margin rate (ex gas and membership fees) fell ~170 bps y/y, mainly from promotions tied to the company's 42nd birthday event.

Adj. SG&A fell 11.5% y/y to $696mn. It includes a ~$240mn benefit (net of legal fees) from a legal settlement, partly offset by ~$95mn of expenses tied to use of the settlement proceeds. Sale-leaseback gains also lowered SG&A. Higher labor, occupancy and operating costs from new clubs and gas stations partly offset this.

Expense ratio was 11.1% (-363 bps y/y) vs GS/consensus 14.1%/13.8%. EBIT margin was 5.0% vs GS/consensus 3.9%. The EBIT and EPS beat therefore rests largely on the one-time settlement benefit and sale-leaseback gains, not on gross margin.
BJ repurchased $35.6mn of stock in the quarter vs GS estimate of $25.0mn.

The stock is down ~6% pre-market. GS will ask on the call about traffic/ticket, 4Q-to-date comps, category detail, member renewal and higher-tier penetration rates, gross margin investments, inflation and the promotional environment.

GS rates BJ Buy with a 12-month price target of $104, based on a risk-reward framework with downside/base/upside relative P/E multiples of 85%/90%/95%. The stock closed at $110.75 on 19 Nov, so the target implies 6.1% downside.

market_movers.rationale: Q3 comps, EBIT and EPS beat and FY26 guidance was raised, but gross margin missed on promotions and the EPS beat includes a ~$240mn legal settlement benefit. Stock is down ~6% pre-market and the $104 target sits below the $110.75 price.

earnings_insights: BJ 3Q26 (reported 11/20): SSS ex gas +4.1% reported vs GS est +2.6% and LSEG consensus +2.8%.
BJ 3Q26 (reported 11/20): adj. EPS $1.73 reported vs GS est $1.26 and LSEG consensus est $1.25. Year-ago adj. EPS was $1.16, so +49.1% y/y.
BJ 3Q26 (reported 11/20): EBIT $314mn reported vs GS est $236mn and consensus est $234mn, +42.7% y/y. EBIT margin 5.0% vs GS/consensus est 3.9%.
BJ 3Q26 total revenue growth was +17.5% y/y vs GS est +12.0%. U.S. retail sales were $6,145mn vs GS est $5,854mn, and membership fees were $138mn vs GS est $135mn.
BJ 3Q26 gross margin incl. membership fees was 16.3% reported vs GS est 18.2% and consensus 18.2%. Gross profit incl. membership fees was $1,025mn vs GS est $1,090mn.
BJ FY26 guidance raised: SSS ex gas +2.5-3.0% (prior +2.0-3.0%, GS est +2.4%, consensus +2.6%) and adj. EPS $5.10-5.30 (prior $4.60-4.80, GS est $4.80, consensus $4.73).
BJ 3Q26 adj. SG&A of $696mn includes a ~$240mn net legal settlement benefit and sale-leaseback gains. The reported EPS beat is therefore not a clean operating beat.
risk_factors: Traffic and sales trends decelerate from weak consumer spending or lost member loyalty to traditional retailers or other club models.
Regional macro weakness or disruption on the US East Coast, especially the NYC metro area (~25% of sales).
Limited in-stock availability from supply chain issues such as freight and port congestion.

tension_points.bull_case: Comps of +4.1% beat GS +2.6% and consensus +2.8%, adj. EPS of $1.73 beat $1.25 consensus, MFI grew +9.5% y/y, and FY26 EPS guidance was raised to $5.10-5.30.
tension_points.bear_case: Gross margin of 16.3% missed the 18.2% estimate on promotions, and the EBIT and EPS beat rests on a ~$240mn legal settlement benefit and sale-leaseback gains in SG&A. The stock is down ~6% pre-market.
tension_points.what_invalidates: GS names call items rather than a level: 4Q-to-date comp trends, member renewal rates and gross margin investments.
